title: Energy-to-XP Efficiency Model
dataSources: Life score (`lifeos:score`), quests / tasks (`quest:task`), habit streaks (`streak:status`), life achievements (`achievement:life`), household leaderboard (`household:leaderboard`), plus every other `index=personal` sourcetype as input.
app: The parody-the-enterprise meta layer — a Personal NOC (house-health wall), Personal SOC (entry / impossible-travel), Personal SRE (SLOs on your own habits), and a gamification layer (XP, achievements, streaks, household leaderboards) — all computed in Splunk over `index=personal`.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=lifeos:score
| stats avg(xp_earned) as avg_xp, avg(energy_score) as avg_energy by domain
| eval xp_per_energy=round(avg_xp/avg_energy,2)
| sort - xp_per_energy
description: Compares how much XP different domains generate per unit of energy invested.
value: Gamification is only useful if rewards reflect reality; energy efficiency shows which domains are truly paying back effort.
implementation: Calculate average XP earned and energy score per domain and derive XP-per-energy ratio.
visualization: Table of domains by XP per energy unit.
grandmaExplanation: It warns which areas of life give you the most progress back for the energy you spend.
